According to standard triangle notation, a denotes BC, and c denotes AB; C in the problem is the quantity to be found and corresponds to the standard answer, so according to the specified method it is interpreted as side c. Given a=1, ∠A=π/6, ∠B=π/4. The third angle is ∠C=π-π/6-π/4=7π/12. By the sine theorem, c/sin∠C = a/sin∠A = 1/sin(π/6)=2. Therefore c=2sin(7π/12). Also sin(7π/12)=sin(5π/12)=sin(π/4+π/6)=sin(π/4)cos(π/6)+cos(π/4)sin(π/6)=√6/4+√2/4, so c=2(√6/4+√2/4)=(√6+√2)/2.

method.method_draft: Use a right-triangle altitude construction. From the text, take a=BC=1, A=30°, B=45°, and seek c=AB. Drop the altitude CD from C to AB. In right triangle BCD, since angle B=45° and BC=1 is the hypotenuse, BD=CD=1/√2=√2/2. In right triangle ACD, angle A=30°, so tan 30°=CD/AD, hence AD=CD/tan 30°=(√2/2)·√3=√6/2. Therefore AB=AD+BD=√6/2+√2/2=(√6+√2)/2.
